full_text_en:
Wang Jimei v. Yizheng Longxing Plastic Co., Ltd. — dispute over right to life

【Ruling Summary】

Pursuant to Article 22 of the Flood Control Law of the People's Republic of China, it is prohibited to construct buildings or structures that impede flood discharge within the management scope of rivers and lakes, and to engage in activities that affect the stability of river regimes, endanger the safety of riverbanks and levees, or otherwise obstruct flood discharge in rivers.

The right to life of citizens is protected by law. A person who infringes upon the civil rights and interests of another person through fault shall bear tort liability. If the victim also has fault for the occurrence of the damage, the tortfeasor's civil liability may be mitigated.

Plaintiff: Wang Jimei, female, 45 years old, residing in Yizheng City, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Yizheng Longxing Plastic Co., Ltd., domiciled at Yonghe Road, Zhenzhou Town, Yizheng City, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Ma Yaozhang, Chairman of the Board of the company.

The plaintiff, Wang Jimei, filed a lawsuit with the Yizheng People's Court against the defendant, Yizheng Longxing Plastic Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Longxing Company), for a dispute over the right to life.

Plaintiff's Allegations: On the afternoon of July 12, 2011, Yizheng City encountered a rainstorm. The plaintiff's daughter, Yang Ying, who was working part-time during the summer vacation, was swept by the surging river water that burst out of a dam into a culvert beside the road while cycling on the auxiliary road of the Ningtong Highway at the Xiayun Group section of Yongqing Village, Zhenzhou Town. It was not until around 11:00 a.m. the next day that the drowned Yang Ying was found in a river two kilometers from the scene. The defendant, Longxing Company, wantonly built a dam in the drainage channel to raise fish, neglected management of the river channel within its factory area, and illegally constructed a wall over the drainage channel. These actions were the main factors causing the plaintiff's daughter's drowning death, and the defendant should bear the primary liability for the accident. The Yizheng Transportation Bureau, as the highway management department, failed to install guardrails at the accident site and should bear joint and several compensation liability for the accident. The Yizheng Water Authority also failed to install guardrails at the culvert facilities and neglected management, and should also bear joint and several compensation liability for the accident. The plaintiff now demands that the defendant, together with the Yizheng Transportation Bureau and the Yizheng Water Authority, jointly and severally compensate for funeral expenses of RMB 20,252.5, death compensation of RMB 526,820, and mental distress damages of RMB 50,000, totaling RMB 597,072.5, and bear the litigation costs of this case.

Defendant's Defense: 1. The death of the plaintiff's daughter was neither caused by the collapse of our company's wall nor by the release of water by our company. It was an accidental drowning due to flash flooding caused by a sudden rainstorm, which constitutes force majeure. 2. The location of the plaintiff's daughter's death was not within the scope of our company's supervision and has no relationship with our company. At the time of this sudden rainstorm and flash flood, our company was also a victim; the upstream water surged straight down, flooding our company's factory buildings and machinery, causing significant losses. 3. Our company constructed a wall for the safety of the enterprise and to prevent drowning accidents. It did not obstruct the waterway but instead fulfilled our duty to keep the waterway unobstructed. Leaving an exit over two meters wide was to avoid disputes with local farmers, not as a water outlet. The construction of the wall on land our company had legally requisitioned has no causal relationship with this accidental death. 4. The plaintiff bears responsibility for failing to properly supervise her daughter. The plaintiff's daughter lacked the most basic awareness of danger prevention and self-rescue, and she should also bear responsibility for this accident. In summary, our company bears no liability for this accident and requests the court to reject the plaintiff's claims against our company.

The Yizheng People's Court found the following facts after trial at first instance:

The plaintiff, Wang Jimei, is the mother of Yang Ying. On the afternoon of July 12, 2011, Yizheng City encountered a rainstorm. At approximately 3:40 p.m. on the same day, while riding an electric bicycle on the north auxiliary road of the Ningtong Highway at the Xiayun Group section of Yongqing Village, Zhenzhou Town, Yang Ying was swept by surging river water into a pond beside the road. She was then swept into a culvert connected to the pond and located beneath the Ningtong Highway. As this culvert was connected to an underground ditch on the west side of Xiyuan Road, the drowned Yang Ying was not discovered until around 11:00 a.m. the next day in the Yanshan River, two kilometers from the accident site.

Xiyuan Road in Yizheng City runs south from the Yanjiang High-Grade Highway and north to the south auxiliary road of the Ningtong Expressway. The north auxiliary road of the Ningtong Expressway runs from east to west before turning north at the Xiayun Group section of Yongqing Village, Zhenzhou Town, becoming a north-south route, and connects to the north section of Xiyuan North Road via a pedestrian culvert beneath the Ningtong Expressway. The accident site is located on the north side of the Ningtong Expressway, on the road connecting the north auxiliary road of the Ningtong Expressway to the north section of Xiyuan North Road. The terrain at this site is low-lying, with a pond to the east. The pond connects to the south with a water-passing culvert beneath the Ningtong Expressway. The terrain west of the accident site is higher. Approximately 100 meters to the northwest lies a north-south river channel. The west side of this river channel is the factory area of the defendant, Longxing Company, which enclosed the river channel within its factory area by building a wall. At the southern end of this river channel, there was a pipe with a diameter of approximately 500mm serving as a water outlet, discharging water to the south. On the day of the incident, a rainstorm occurred. The swollen river water rushed through the wall at the southern end of the river channel, poured onto the road across the ground, and caused the drowning death of Yang Ying, who was passing by on her bicycle.

During the trial of this case, the plaintiff, Wang Jimei, reached settlement agreements with the Yizheng Transportation Bureau on January 29, 2013, and with the Yizheng Water Authority on February 17, 2013. Each defendant compensated the plaintiff RMB 90,000, totaling RMB 180,000 (equivalent to 30% of the total compensation amount claimed by the plaintiff). The plaintiff applied to withdraw the claims for compensation liability against the Yizheng Transportation Bureau and the Yizheng Water Authority, and the court ruled to permit the withdrawal.

The Yizheng People's Court held at first instance:

The issues in dispute at first instance were: First, whether the defendant, Longxing Company, should bear compensation liability; Second, if the defendant, Longxing Company, should bear compensation liability, how the compensation share should be determined.

The right to life of citizens is protected by law. A person who infringes upon the civil rights and interests of another person through fault shall bear tort liability.

Regarding the first issue, Article 22 of the Flood Control Law of the People's Republic of China provides that it is prohibited to construct buildings or structures that impede flood discharge within the management scope of rivers and lakes, and to engage in activities that affect the stability of river regimes, endanger the safety of riverbanks and levees, or otherwise obstruct flood discharge in rivers. The defendant, Longxing Company, without authorization, illegally constructed a wall to enclose part of the river channel within its factory area and set up nets at the north and south ends for fish farming, causing obstruction to the flood discharge of that river section. This was the main reason that ultimately led to the flood destroying the wall and rushing out, resulting in the drowning death of the victim, Yang Ying. Force majeure refers to objective circumstances that are unforeseeable, unavoidable, and insurmountable, excluding human factors. The defendant should have foreseen that its illegal actions left a safety hazard for residents near this river section. Therefore, the defendant's defense that the accident constituted force majeure and that it should not bear compensation liability lacks legal basis, and the court does not accept it. The plaintiff's claim for the defendant to bear compensation liability is supported by the court.

Regarding the second issue, the victim, Yang Ying, as a high school student, should have had a certain cognitive ability and awareness of self-safety precautions regarding ordinary matters. On July 12, 2011, a rainstorm occurred. After the floodwater burst through the wall of Longxing Company at the southern end of the river channel, it formed a swift current on the north auxiliary road of the Ningtong Expressway. Many passersby took detours. Yang Ying, who was familiar with the road conditions, ignored the advice of others and failed to confirm safety before cycling through the accident site, which was also one of the causes of the accident. Where the victim also has fault for the occurrence of the damage, the civil liability of the infringer may be mitigated. Given that the Yizheng Transportation Bureau and the Yizheng Water Authority have already assumed 30% of the compensation liability, the court, based on the relative weight of the causes of the accident, determined that the defendant, Longxing Company, should bear 40% of the compensation liability, and the plaintiff, Wang Jimei, should bear 30% of the liability herself.

Regarding the specific amount of compensation claimed by the plaintiff, Wang Jimei, the court determined the following in accordance with the scope, items, and standards stipulated in the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Personal Injury Compensation Cases: funeral expenses of RMB 22,993.5, death compensation of RMB 526,820, and mental distress damages of RMB 35,000, totaling RMB 584,813.5. The defendant, Longxing Company, shall compensate the plaintiff, Wang Jimei, in the amount of RMB 239,925.4 [(RMB 584,813.5 - RMB 35,000) × 40% + (RMB 35,000 ÷ 70%) × 40%].

In summary, in accordance with Articles 98, 119, and 131 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China; Articles 2, 16, 22, and 26 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China; and Articles 17, 18, 27, and 29 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Personal Injury Compensation Cases, the Yizheng People's Court rendered the following judgment on March 17, 2013:

The defendant, Yizheng Longxing Plastic Co., Ltd., shall pay the plaintiff, Wang Jimei, RMB 239,925.4 within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment.

Longxing Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, filed an appeal to the Yangzhou Intermediate People's Court, contending: 1. The location of the drowning death of the appellee's daughter was not within the appellant's factory area. The incident occurred because the victim refused to heed others' advice and acted willfully. As the victim was a minor, the appellee was negligent in supervision. 2. The accident was caused by flash flooding resulting from a sudden rainstorm, which constitutes force majeure. In summary, the appellant requests the court of second instance to amend the judgment.

The appellee, Wang Jimei, did not submit a defense.

During the second instance, neither the appellant nor the appellee submitted new evidence to the court.

After trial at second instance, the Yangzhou Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The Yangzhou Intermediate People's Court held at second instance:

Although the sudden rainstorm due to weather conditions was a natural phenomenon, the appellant, Longxing Company, had constructed a wall, causing upstream river water to be retained within the company's factory area until a portion of the wall was breached, causing water to rush rapidly towards the roadside. This was one of the significant factors contributing to the sweeping away and drowning of Yang Ying, the daughter of the appellee, Wang Jimei. Therefore, Yang Ying's death was not caused by force majeure. The court of first instance correctly determined that Longxing Company should bear 40% of the compensation liability, and the apportionment was appropriate. The appellant argued that Yang Ying should bear corresponding liability for ignoring others' advice and acting willfully, and that her guardian, Wang Jimei, had failed to fulfill her supervisory duties. The court of first instance had already determined that the appellee should bear 30% of the liability herself, which complies with the law. The court does not support the appellant's claim that the appellee should bear more liability.

In summary, the appellant's contentions lack factual and legal basis and are not supported. The judgment of first instance had clear findings of fact, correct application of law, and lawful procedures, and should be affirmed. Accordingly, in accordance with Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Yangzhou Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on July 20, 2013:

Appeal dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
